note: PSMA (FOLH1)-directed payload delivery was built on PSMA-positive versus PSMA-negative prostate tumour-bearing mice; the radioligands (131I-MIP-1095, 177Lu-PSMA-617) matched the uptake and response predictions but the mice missed the salivary-gland harm, and the MMAE antibody-drug conjugate fell short of its xenograft regressions.
label: Prostate cancer (PSMA depleters)

engagement.model: PSMA-positive (LNCaP) vs PSMA-negative (PC3) xenograft biodistribution in mice
engagement.note: Radioiodinated MIP-1095 accumulated in LNCaP but not PC3 xenografts and was displaced by PMPA; the targeting model for the small-molecule radioligands.
engagement.quote: Specific binding to PSMA in vivo was shown by competition with PMPA in LNCaP xenografts, and the absence of uptake in PC3 xenografts.
engagement.judgement: Opens the radioligand track: the same PSMA-positive/PSMA-negative tumour-bearing mouse system (LNCaP vs PC3 here; PC-3 PIP vs PC-3 flu in Umbricht 2017; RM1-hPSMA in Fendler 2017) carried every small-molecule radioligand, so MIP-1095 and PSMA-617 share one track; the antibody-drug conjugate's castrate CRPC xenografts are a different model with a different prediction and get their own track.

engagement.model: PSMA-positive (LNCaP) vs PSMA-negative (PC3) xenograft biodistribution in mice
engagement.note: 124I-MIP-1095 PET in 16 patients showed excellent tumour uptake, the direct read-out the LNCaP/PC3 mice had predicted.
engagement.short: Tumour uptake confirmed by patient PET
engagement.quote: I-124-MIP-1095 PET/CT images showed excellent tumor uptake and moderate uptake in liver, proximal intestine and within a few hours post-injection also in the kidneys.
engagement.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading; the paper reports human biodistribution without printing the mouse numbers beside it, so this is a pairing with Hillier 2009.
engagement.judgement: Direct readout: the radioligand itself is imaged in tumour. Compassionate-use series, no registry record, so registry_date is null. The same ligand (MIP-1095) was the one dosed in the mice, product_in_model true.

engagement.model: PSMA-positive (LNCaP) vs PSMA-negative (PC3) xenograft biodistribution in mice
engagement.note: 177Lu-PSMA-617: patients were chosen on PSMA imaging, as the PSMA-dependent uptake in LNCaP mice implied; 13 of 30 had >50% PSA falls.
engagement.short: PSMA imaging selected responders, PSA fell
engagement.quote: Patients with PSMA-positive tumor phenotypes were selected by molecular imaging.
engagement.reason: Patient PSMA uptake matched the mice
engagement.judgement: Patient-level use of the model's rule (uptake tracks PSMA expression): VISION later screened 1003 men by 68Ga-PSMA-11 PET and excluded 3% with no PSMA-positive lesion and 9% with a PSMA-negative lesion (FDA review NDA 215833, https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2022/215833Orig1s000MultidisciplineR.pdf). Benešová 2015 (doi 10.2967/jnumed.114.147413) is the PSMA-617 mouse paper and is cited in the NDA, so model_filed is true for this entry. registry_date is VISION's results posting.

engagement.model: Docetaxel-refractory PSMA-high CRPC xenografts dosed with PSMA ADC
engagement.note: PSMA ADC killed cells with >100,000 PSMA molecules per cell 1,000-fold more efficiently than PSMA-null cells: a threshold rule for who responds.
engagement.short: Killing needed abundant PSMA per cell
engagement.quote: In vitro cell killing was efficient for cells with abundant PSMA expression (>10(5) molecules/cell; IC(50) ≤ 0.022 nmol/L) and 1,000-fold less efficient for cells with undetectable PSMA (IC(50) > 30 nmol/L).
engagement.judgement: Separate track from the radioligand mice: a different model (castrate C4-2 and LuCaP patient-derived xenografts, DiPippo 2015 doi 10.1002/pros.22916) dosed with the product itself, predicting regression and a PSMA-expression threshold rather than uptake.

engagement.model: Docetaxel-refractory PSMA-high CRPC xenografts dosed with PSMA ADC
engagement.note: In 119 mCRPC patients, PSA and CTC falls tracked PSMA expression on CTCs or tissue, the threshold rule the cell and PDX work had set.
engagement.short: Response tracked PSMA expression in patients
engagement.quote: PSA and CTC reductions were associated with high PSMA expression (CTCs or tumor tissue) and low neuroendocrine serum markers.
engagement.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading; downstream read-out (PSA, CTC), and the paper does not print the model data beside it.
engagement.reason: PSMA-high patients responded, PSMA-low did not
engagement.judgement: Year is the phase 2 registry results posting (NCT01695044, 2017-02-23), earlier than the paper (epub 2019-11-19, print 2020); the peer-reviewed paper sets the status. Trials were PSMA-unselected, so the patient-level rule was tested inside an unselected population.

dose.model: LNCaP xenograft biodistribution of 177Lu-PSMA-617 in mice
dose.note: Mouse kidneys took up 113% ID/g at 1 h but cleared to 2% by 24 h while tumour held: the stated therapeutic window.
dose.quote: With regard to therapeutic use, the compound exhibited a rapid clearance from the kidneys from 113.3 ± 24.4 at 1 h to 2.13 ± 1.36 percentage injected dose per gram at 24 h.
dose.judgement: The mouse gave no activity target in human units; its dose prediction is the kidney-clearance margin, so the dose cell is scored on that margin (decision 16).

dose.model: LNCaP xenograft biodistribution of 177Lu-PSMA-617 in mice
dose.note: The mouse-derived low kidney uptake was the reason for choosing PSMA-617; human dosimetry over 1-3 cycles bore it out with PSA responses.
dose.short: Low kidney dose held in patients
dose.quote: Besides high affinity and long tumor retention, the DOTA-conjugated ligand PSMA-617 has low kidney uptake, making it an excellent choice for therapeutic application.
dose.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading; the human kidney absorbed dose is in the full text.
dose.judgement: The source states the model-derived property as the reason for the therapeutic choice and reports human dosimetry, so comparison_stated is true. Margin: the model said the kidney clears; it did. Whether the dose was enough waited for VISION (next entry).

dose.model: LNCaP xenograft biodistribution of 177Lu-PSMA-617 in mice
dose.note: 6 x 7.4 GBq gave kidneys 19 Gy, under the 23 Gy convention; the regimen was reached and VISION showed it was enough.
dose.short: Kidney 19 Gy over six cycles; worked
dose.quote: On average, the kidneys received 0.43 (SD=0.16) Gy/GBq, which for a full six cycle cumulative administration of 44.4 GBq, results in a calculated estimated absorbed dose to the kidneys of 19 (SD=7.3) Gy.
dose.reason: Regimen reached, kidney margin held, drug worked
dose.judgement: The review puts the rodent finding (kidney uptake that decreased over time) and the 29-patient dosimetry sub-study in one document; the 7.4 GBq x 6 regimen came from human dosimetry and phase 2, not from the mice, which is why the model's only dose claim is the margin. Salivary/lacrimal glands, not kidneys, took the highest absorbed doses (0.63 and 2.1 Gy/GBq), a harm the mice did not predict; counted once, in safety. Grade 3-4 acute kidney injury 3% with follow-up too short for late nephrotoxicity (post-marketing requirement).
dose.magnitude_basis: kidney absorbed dose vs 23 Gy convention

dose.model: Docetaxel-refractory PSMA-high CRPC xenografts dosed with PSMA ADC
dose.note: Mice regressed on 1-6 mg/kg weekly with no stated tolerability margin; the clinic capped the dose at 2.5 mg/kg q3w on neutropenia and neuropathy.
dose.quote: PSMA ADC showed high in vivo activity in treating xenograft tumors that had progressed following an initial course of docetaxel therapy, including tumors that were large (>700 mm(3)) before treatment with PSMA ADC.
dose.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading of the model papers; no exposure target or tolerated dose is stated in either abstract.
dose.judgement: Phase 1 (Petrylak 2019, doi 10.1002/pros.23765; NCT01414283, no results posted) set the MTD at 2.5 mg/kg q3w with neutropenia and peripheral neuropathy as dose-limiting, below the 6 mg/kg weekly regimen DiPippo 2015 used in LuCaP PDX. With no stated margin this is the 'never reached because of toxicity, no stated margin' row: untested here, and the clinical failure is counted once, in efficacy.

efficacy.model: PSMA-positive vs PSMA-negative prostate tumour-bearing mice
efficacy.note: LNCaP xenografts took up 34% ID/g of 123I-MIP-1095 at 4 h; an imaging model, with therapy studies in PSMA-positive mice to follow.
efficacy.short: Imaging model; therapy studies came later
efficacy.quote: Tissue distribution studies in mice showed 17.3 +/- 6.3% (at 1 hour) and 34.3 +/- 12.7% (at 4 hours) injected dose per gram of LNCaP xenograft tissue, for [(123)I]MIP-1072 and [(123)I]MIP-1095, respectively.
efficacy.judgement: Therapy in the same system came with 177Lu-PSMA-617: RM1-hPSMA syngeneic mice (Fendler 2017, doi 10.2967/jnumed.117.193359; up to 85% growth inhibition and longer survival at 120 MBq per the FDA review) and PSMA-positive PC-3 PIP cells (Müller 2019, cited in the review). Same system, same prediction, one track.

efficacy.model: PSMA-positive vs PSMA-negative prostate tumour-bearing mice
efficacy.note: VISION: in 831 PSMA-PET-selected mCRPC patients, 177Lu-PSMA-617 cut radiographic progression (HR 0.40) and death (alternate primary), as PSMA-positive mice predicted.
efficacy.quote: 177Lu-PSMA-617 plus standard care significantly prolonged, as compared with standard care, both imaging-based progression-free survival (median, 8.7 vs. 3.4 months; hazard ratio for progression or death, 0.40; 99.2% confidence interval [CI], 0.29 to 0.57
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading of the trial paper; the quote is the abstract sentence cut at the CI.
efficacy.judgement: Pairing of the RM1-hPSMA therapy model with VISION; the FDA review (tier 2) puts both in one document but states the literature models were 'not used for labeling recommendations', so regulatory_reliance stays false. 131I-MIP-1095 is scored on this track too: ARROW (NCT03939689, results posted 2025-10-14; Clin Cancer Res 2026) met its PSA50 primary endpoint, 62.9% vs 31.3%, with rPFS/OS unpowered and not improved and two treatment-related deaths; the registry lists it completed, not stopped, so it is a match on the primary endpoint with a negative outcome signal, listed under patient_trials and not a contra. PSMAfore (taxane-naive) and TheraP repeated the pattern.

patient_trials.quote: the median radiographic progression-free survival was 9·30 months (95% CI 6·77-not estimable) in the 177Lu-PSMA-617 group versus 5·55 months (4·04-5·95) in the ARPI change group (hazard ratio [HR] 0·41 [95% CI 0·29-0·56]; p<0·0001)
PSA50 response was 62.9% [95% confidence interval (CI), 50.5-74.1] for 131I-LNTH-1095 + enzalutamide versus 31.3% (16.1-50) for enzalutamide alone (P = 0.003).
PSA responses were more frequent among men in the [177Lu]Lu-PSMA-617 group than in the cabazitaxel group (65 vs 37 PSA responses; 66% vs 37% by intention to treat
17 (57%) of 30 patients (95% CI 37-75) achieved a PSA decline of 50% or more

efficacy.model: PSMA-positive vs PSMA-negative prostate tumour-bearing mice
efficacy.note: Patient-level: PSMA-PET SUVmean >=10 predicted PSA response to 177Lu-PSMA-617 over cabazitaxel (91% vs 47%), the uptake-tracks-PSMA rule from PC-3 PIP/flu mice.
efficacy.quote: In men with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer, PSMA-PET SUVmean was predictive of higher likelihood of favourable response to [177Lu]Lu-PSMA-617 than cabazitaxel, which provides guidance for optimal [177Lu]Lu-PSMA-617 use.
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading; prespecified tertiary endpoint of a randomised trial, so endpoint_role is null.
efficacy.reason: Mice predicted the class; PET picks patients
efficacy.judgement: Treatment-by-SUVmean interaction padj=0.039. The patient-level comparison the tile asked for: the isogenic PSMA-positive/negative pair (Umbricht 2017) says uptake, hence kill, follows PSMA level; TheraP shows the same rule stratifies human response. TheraP has no ClinicalTrials.gov results record (ANZCTR primary), registry_date null.

efficacy.model: Docetaxel-refractory PSMA-high CRPC xenografts dosed with PSMA ADC
efficacy.note: PSMA ADC regressed large docetaxel-progressed xenografts; LuCaP PDX later ranged from complete regression to no effect by PSMA level.
efficacy.quote: PSMA ADC showed high in vivo activity in treating xenograft tumors that had progressed following an initial course of docetaxel therapy, including tumors that were large (>700 mm(3)) before treatment with PSMA ADC.
efficacy.judgement: DiPippo 2015 (doi 10.1002/pros.22916) added the PDX panel: complete regressions in LuCaP 96CR, unimpeded growth in low-PSMA LuCaP 58, and 'considerable variability in effects despite PSMA expression'.

efficacy.model: Docetaxel-refractory PSMA-high CRPC xenografts dosed with PSMA ADC
efficacy.note: At the 2.5 mg/kg MTD, PSA fell >=50% in 14% of 113 patients, best response stable disease in 61% post-chemotherapy; program dropped.
efficacy.quote: PSA declines ≥50% occurred in 14% of all treated (n = 113) and 21% of chemotherapy-naïve subjects (n = 34).
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading; the phase 2 primary measure was antitumour activity by PSA and CTC decline, treated here as the primary endpoint.
efficacy.judgement: The model predicted regression of docetaxel-refractory tumours; patients at the toxicity-capped dose gave partial responses in 5.7% (chemotherapy-naive) and stable disease at best after chemotherapy, and the sponsor took the ADC no further. Year is the registry results posting (NCT01695044, 2017-02-23); the paper sets the status. The patient-level half of the prediction (response tracks PSMA level) held and is scored in engagement. No single-species scaling makes 2.5 mg/kg q3w equal to 6 mg/kg weekly, but with no stated margin the dose cell stays untested and the failure is counted here once.
efficacy.magnitude_basis: PSA50 response rate vs xenograft regression

safety.model: PSMA-positive vs PSMA-negative xenograft biodistribution in mice
safety.note: Mouse biodistribution ranked kidney as the normal organ taking up PSMA ligand; no patient organ-dose comparison yet.
safety.short: Mouse organ ranking not yet compared
safety.quote: [(123)I]MIP-1095 exhibited greater tumor uptake but slower washout from blood and nontarget tissues compared with [(123)I]MIP-1072.
safety.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading; the organ table is in the full text.
safety.judgement: The ligand-only rat and minipig toxicology filed for Pluvicto (cold 175Lu-PSMA-617, no radiation) predicted no ligand-mediated harm and the review attributes every clinical harm to radiation; no quotable side-by-side, so it is not scored as a track.

safety.model: PSMA-positive vs PSMA-negative xenograft biodistribution in mice
safety.note: In men the salivary glands, not kidneys, took the highest absorbed dose (3.8 mSv/MBq) and 25% got dry mouth; the mice had flagged kidney.
safety.short: Salivary glands, not kidney, took most dose
safety.quote: Dosimetry estimates for I-131-MIP-1095 revealed that the highest absorbed doses were delivered to the salivary glands (3.8 mSv/MBq, liver (1.7 mSv/MBq) and kidneys (1.4 mSv/MBq).
safety.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading; pairing with Hillier 2009, whose abstract reports tumour, blood and non-target washout but no salivary signal.
safety.judgement: On-target harm, so pooled rather than per modality. Mouse salivary glands carry far less PSMA than human (Roy 2020, next entry) and the human gland uptake is largely non-PSMA-mediated (Rupp 2019, doi 10.2967/jnumed.118.222307), so the species could not rank the organ at risk: kidney in mouse, salivary/lacrimal gland in man. Compassionate-use series, no registry record.
safety.magnitude_basis: organ-at-risk ranking: mouse kidney vs human salivary/lacrimal glands

safety.model: PSMA-positive vs PSMA-negative xenograft biodistribution in mice
safety.note: Species comparison: rodent submandibular PSMA is the lowest of all species tested, so rodents cannot forecast the xerostomia seen in 39% of VISION patients.
safety.short: Rodent salivary PSMA lowest; xerostomia missed
safety.quote: Rodents had the lowest SMG PSMA levels, with the mouse being 10-fold higher than the rat.
safety.judgement: Stated comparison of human, monkey and rodent salivary PSMA with in vivo rodent biodistribution. VISION: dry mouth 38.8% vs 0.5% on standard care alone; the 29-patient sub-study gave lacrimal 2.1 and salivary 0.63 Gy/GBq against kidney 0.43 (FDA review NDA 215833). Kratochwil 2016 had already reported xerostomia with 177Lu-PSMA-617. Myelosuppression and thrombocytopenia (51% grade >=3 TEAE rate in ARROW's combination arm) are generic radiation harms the cold-ligand toxicology could not show.
safety.magnitude_basis: submandibular PSMA level, rodent vs human

safety.model: Docetaxel-refractory PSMA-high CRPC xenografts dosed with PSMA ADC
safety.note: Efficacy xenografts with no toxicology read-out; silent on the MMAE payload's neutropenia and neuropathy.
safety.quote: In contrast, less potent and nonselective cytotoxic activity was observed for a control ADC, free monomethylauristatin E, and other microtubule inhibitors.
safety.judgement: Platform (payload) harms are split by modality under the tile's two modality groups.

safety.model: Docetaxel-refractory PSMA-high CRPC xenografts dosed with PSMA ADC
safety.note: Neutropenia and peripheral neuropathy capped the dose and two patients at 2.5 mg/kg died of sepsis: the vc-MMAE platform harms brentuximab vedotin had shown.
safety.quote: Two subjects who received 2.5 mg/kg died of sepsis.
safety.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading; the platform comparator (Younes 2010, brentuximab vedotin phase 1 in CD30-positive lymphoma) is not named in the abstract, so this is a pairing.
safety.reason: Platform harms seen with brentuximab vedotin
safety.judgement: Off-target payload harm, so 'other' (same platform only, decision 13): the vc-MMAE conjugate brentuximab vedotin had shown peripheral neuropathy and neutropenia in 2010 (doi 10.1056/NEJMoa1002965). Phase 1 (Petrylak 2019) named neutropenia and peripheral neuropathy as the first-cycle and late dose-limiting toxicities. Year is the phase 2 registry results posting (2017-02-23). imported_from is left null: the comparator indication is CD30-positive lymphoma and I did not verify its MONDO id in-session.

safety.model: GLP single-dose rat and minipig and 4-week repeat-dose rat toxicology of unlabelled PSMA-617 / non-radioactive 175Lu-PSMA-617 (cold ligand)
safety.note: GLP single-dose rat and minipig and 4-week rat studies of the cold ligand filed with the NDA; no patient comparison drawn before the review.
safety.quote: The ligand-mediated toxicities of 177Lu-PSMA-617 were assessed in single-dose toxicity studies in rats and minipigs using a 1:1 mixture of non-radioactive 175Lu-PSMA-617 and unlabeled PSMA-617
safety.confidence_note: Proxy year: NDA 215833 received 2021-07-29; the study dates sit in section 5.5 (pp. 42-50), which the text bundle does not carry, and the PDF download returned a 420-byte stub. Quote is from 5.1, the FDA's Assessment.
safety.judgement: Own track: a different system (healthy rats and minipigs given the non-radioactive ligand) making a different prediction (ligand-mediated, not PSMA-targeting, harm) from the tumour-bearing mice. A platform harm of the radioligand modality, so modality 'other', kept apart from the ADC's vc-MMAE payload harms. Opens untested at first use per the brief; the comparison is the next entry.

safety.model: GLP single-dose rat and minipig and 4-week repeat-dose rat toxicology of unlabelled PSMA-617 / non-radioactive 175Lu-PSMA-617 (cold ligand)
safety.note: Rat and minipig cold-ligand studies predicted no ligand-mediated harm; the review attributes VISION's toxicities (dry mouth 39%, myelosuppression, nausea, renal) to radiation.
safety.short: No ligand harm predicted; none seen
safety.quote: Single dose IV administration of 175Lu-PSMA-617 and unlabeled PSMA-617 caused no toxicologic
safety.confidence_note: The bundle's text ends this sentence at a page break ('caused no toxicologic ...'); the section 5.5 tables (rat A3732, minipig A3733, pp. 45-46) are absent and the PDF could not be re-fetched. The clinical side, 8.2.1 'the main expected toxicities of 177Lu-PSMA-617 are related to radiation damage to normal tissues', sits in the applicant's section of the review.
safety.reason: Ligand null held; harms were radiation
safety.judgement: Stated null prediction (#58) that held: the review's nonclinical executive summary (5.1, The FDA's Assessment) records no toxicologic findings for the cold ligand in rat and minipig, and its safety review attributes every frequent VISION harm (dry mouth 38.8%, myelosuppression, nausea, acute kidney injury) to radiation on PSMA-expressing, adjacent or clearing tissues; no ligand-mediated harm was identified. Scored same, direction only, as a platform harm of the radioligand (modality 'other'); the on-target salivary miss stays on the xenograft track. Not a retrodiction: the GLP studies were filed 2021-07-29, before the review drew the comparison. Dated 2022, when the review became public with the 2022-03-23 approval; registry_date is VISION's results posting (NCT03511664).
safety.magnitude_basis: ligand-mediated (non-radiation) toxicity: none predicted in rat and minipig, none attributed in VISION

safety.model: Ex-vivo human submandibular-gland tissue: 177Lu-PSMA-617 autoradiography and PSMA immunohistochemistry against the same patients' 68Ga-PSMA-11 PET
safety.note: Submandibular-gland tissue from 9 patients: 177Lu-PSMA-617 autoradiography and PSMA IHC, built to explain the salivary uptake already seen in treated men.
safety.quote: The aim of this study was to investigate whether the accumulation of PSMA-targeting radioligands in submandibular glands (SMGs) can be explained with PSMA expression levels using autoradiography (ARG) and immunohistochemistry (IHC).
safety.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading (PubMed record PMID 30737300, epub 2019-02-08). Opener for a model whose comparison is in the same paper; retrodiction is carried on the scored entry.
safety.judgement: Own track: patient tissue ex vivo (model_kind ex_vivo), not a tumour-bearing mouse, and its prediction is about the organ at risk (is gland uptake PSMA-mediated?), not about PSMA-dependent tumour targeting. Same-year opener per the brief: each cell opens untested at first use.
safety.population: Prostate cancer, PSMA-PET imaged (primary and recurrent)

safety.model: Ex-vivo human submandibular-gland tissue: 177Lu-PSMA-617 autoradiography and PSMA immunohistochemistry against the same patients' 68Ga-PSMA-11 PET
safety.note: Gland tissue showed focal ductal PSMA and 1.3% autoradiography signal, yet the same men's glands took SUVmax 23.5 on PSMA-PET: in-vivo uptake not reproduced.
safety.short: Ex-vivo gland signal minimal; PET uptake high
safety.quote: Our results indicate that the high accumulation of PSMA radioligands in salivary glands does not correspond to high PSMA expression levels determined using ARG and IHC.
safety.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading. The in-vivo side is 68Ga-PSMA-11 PET (SUVmax 23.5 +/- 5.2 in all SMGs), not 177Lu-PSMA-617 therapy; the harm itself (xerostomia) is the draft's Zechmann 2014 / Kratochwil 2016 record, public before the model. No registry record: a tissue study, not a trial.
safety.reason: Failed to reproduce known salivary uptake
safety.judgement: Retrodiction (decision 10): built after the salivary harm was known (Zechmann 2014 dosimetry, 25% dry mouth; VISION later 39%) to test whether PSMA expression explains it, and it failed to reproduce the in-vivo uptake, so contra, never retro. The source states the discordance itself (comparison_stated true) and reads it as a non-PSMA uptake mechanism rather than as a model failure; the atlas scores the model's readout against the patients' and records the source's framing as 'miss'. Magnitude 'opposite': minimal signal ex vivo against high accumulation in vivo. Rupp's patients were primary and recurrent disease; the harm is organ physiology within the same MONDO disease, so no imported_from. Rule question 4 (whether the mouse track's salivary contra stands) is the adjudicator's; this entry does not change it.
safety.magnitude_basis: submandibular-gland radioligand signal: 1.3% of a PSMA-positive standard ex vivo vs SUVmax 23.5 in vivo
safety.population: Prostate cancer, PSMA-PET imaged (primary and recurrent)
